text: . The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. The sixth round of India-Ecuador Foreign Office Consultations was held in New Delhi yesterday. The Indian delegation was led by Secretary (East), MEA, Rudrendra Tandon and the Ecuadorian delegation was led by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility of Ecuador, Alejandro Davalos. The External Affairs Ministry said that the two sides reviewed the progress of bilateral relations and exchanged views on regional and global developments. During his visit to India, Mr Davalos held bilateral meetings with the Commerce Secretary, Health Secretary, and Secretary of the Department of Pharmaceuticals. He also met with Indian business fora.

. Union Health Minister J P Nadda today addressed the inaugural BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting in Colombo highlighting India’s progress towards Universal Health Coverage through Ayushman Bharat, strengthened public health infrastructure and digital healthcare initiatives.Emphasizing regional solidarity, the Minister called for enhanced cooperation in health security, pandemic preparedness, One Health and traditional medicine, while reaffirming India’s readiness to share its expertise and best practices with BIMSTEC member nations.Mr. Nadda also highlighted India’s commitment to hosting the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar, Gujarat, to promote joint research, capacity building and knowledge exchange. Guided by PM Modi’s vision of ‘One Earth, One Family, One Future’, India remains committed to building a healthier, more inclusive and resilient BIMSTEC region.Established in 1997, BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) is a regional grouping of seven countries – India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar and Thailand – aimed at strengthening cooperation between South and South-east Asia. Public health is one of its key areas of cooperation. The first BIMSTEC Senior Officials Meeting on Health was held in Colombo on November 10, 2026, reviewing regional collaboration in disease surveillance, cancer care, traditional medicine and health capacity building, ahead of the inaugural Health Ministers’ Meeting.

. In the Under-19 Asia Cup Cricket, India secured a place in the semi-finals after defeating the United Arab Emirates by 70 runs at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman today.Put into bat first, India set a target of 310 runs and then restricted the UAE to 239 runs in 50 overs. India had scored 309 losing 7 wickets in 50 overs.India’s Aryavir Sehwag was named Player of the Match for his impressive knock of 160 off 168 balls. India will now take on Afghanistan in the semi-final on Thursday.

. The third One-Day International between India and New Zealand was abandoned due to rain at Seddon Park today. India had won the toss and elected to bowl in the rain-affected match. The umpires called off the game as persistent showers prevented play, despite preparations for a 40-over contest. India continue to lead the five-match series 2-nil. The remaining two matches will be played in Tauranga on November 13 and 15. Shubman Gill and KL Rahul will join India’s Test squad in Wellington. Shreyas Iyer will lead the side in the final two ODIs. Ruturaj Gaikwad and Ishan Kishan are expected to feature in the playing eleven.

. In men’s cricket, India suffered a three-wicket defeat to Pakistan in their Group A clash of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman this evening.Batting first, India were bowled out for 208, powered by Arjun Rajput’s 107 off 85 balls. For Pakistan, Rizwanullah, Ali Raza, and Niqab Shafiq each picked up three wickets.In reply, Pakistan chased down the target, losing seven wickets in 48.1 overs, with the help of Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten 100 off 108 balls. For India, Manal Chauhan took three wickets, while Mohit Ulva scalped two.Earlier, India had won the toss and elected to bat first.

. In the forex market today,  the rupee depreciated marginally to trade at 93.94 rupees against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.82 in intra-day trade.

. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has asserted that the United States and Israel are confronting political fallout stemming from military conflicts. Mr. Pezeshkian left Tehran for Turkiye today to attend the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), describing the summit as an important opportunity to discuss regional issues and the environmental damage caused by aggressors.Speaking before his departure, the Iranian leader noted that 196 nations are participating in the summit, with 71 delegations headed by Presidents or Prime Ministers. He indicated that he would utilize the event to address the ecological devastation inflicted upon Tehran and neighboring territories by Washington and Tel Aviv.

. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) will remain closed tomorrow on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. Trading or settlement activities will remain suspended across market segments including equities, equity derivatives, and currency derivatives. However, the commodity segment will observe a partial trading holiday. The Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session but will resume trading in the evening session from 5:00 PM onwards.

. International Master Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh has won the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in Philippines to become India’s 100th Grandmaster and the first from his state to achieve the title. Shrivatri secured the title after scoring seven points from his final eight games, following a defeat in the opening round. The achievement was particularly significant as chess enthusiasts in India had been awaiting the country’s 100th Grandmaster, while Madhya Pradesh had been waiting for its first player to earn the prestigious title.All India Chess Federation President Nitin Narang has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Grandmaster. He described the achievement as a historic milestone and a proud moment for Indian chess, expressing hope that the country would reach 200 Grandmasters next.

. The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) has proposed a new registration framework to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said that the framework has clearly defined pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment and transition to regular registration.The Ministry said that the proposed framework aims to bring greater uniformity, transparency and accountability to professional registration. It also aims to create structured opportunities for eligible practitioners to enhance their qualifications and competencies in accordance with prescribed standards.The key features of the proposed regulations include standardised eligibility criteria and procedures for provisional registration, online application, verification and issuance of registration certificates with unique identification numbers and others. The NCAHP has invited comments, suggestions and objections from allied and healthcare professionals, and others till 4th of December as part of its commitment to transparent and participatory regulation.

. Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal has said that all six Indian seafarers aboard Liberia-flagged VLCC MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY are safe following a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf yesterday.In a social media post, Mr. Sonowal said that the vessel was travelling from Al Ruwais to Dubai when it was hit by a projectile. He informed that four crew members sustained injuries, including one Indian national, who suffered minor injuries and has been safely taken ashore for further medical examination. The Minister further said that the remaining 18 crew members are safe. He added that India is closely monitoring the situation and is in contact with the ship management company to ensure the safety and well-being of Indian seafarers.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. In shooting, India’s Niveditha Veloor Nair secured a bronze medal in the women’s 25-metre standard pistol at the ISSF World Championship in Doha, Qatar, yesterday. Niveditha finished third with a score of 567-13x.China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan won gold while Hungary’s Veronika Major claimed silver with. India’s Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar finished eighth and 10th, respectively.In the team event, the Indian trio of Niveditha Nair, Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar secured silver with a combined score of 1,682-33x. With this, India’s overall tally at the Doha championship has risen to seven, comprising one gold, five silver and one bronze.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. India has urged developed countries to fulfil their climate finance obligations under the Paris Agreement, stressing that financial support is essential to help developing nations tackle climate change. Delivering India’s opening statement at the ongoing UN Climate Conference, COP31, in Antalya, Turkey, Environment Ministry Secretary Narendra Bhooshan said public funding from developed countries remains crucial for climate action in developing nations. He emphasised that developed countries must meet their obligations under Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement, which requires them to provide financial resources to developing countries.India also reaffirmed its commitment to international climate cooperation, calling for a fair and equitable outcome at the conference. The country stressed the importance of the principle of ‘Common But Differentiated Responsibilities’, which recognises that developed and developing nations have different responsibilities and capacities in tackling climate change. India also warned that the growing risk of global warming crossing the 1.5-degree Celsius threshold makes climate justice and equity more urgent than ever.New Delhi highlighted the challenges of ensuring a just transition to clean energy and meeting the adaptation needs of developing countries, particularly those in the Global South.The two-week COP31 conference began on Monday in Antalya, with its President, Murat Kurum, urging countries to turn climate commitments into concrete action. He said the conference should focus on implementation and deliver tangible benefits to people’s lives.Meanwhile, a 2026 report by the UN Environment Programme estimates that developing countries will need around 305 billion dollars every year by 2035 to meet their climate adaptation requirements. However, international public finance from developed countries remains far below the estimated requirement.

. Defending champions India will eye a comprehensive win when they take on Maldives in their second and final group match of the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) Championships in Dhaka today.India beat Pakistan 3-2 in their opening Group B match on the 5th of this month, with Suhail Bhatt scoring a first-half brace. A draw today would be enough to not just make the last four but also top the group.India is competing with a second-string squad as the first team is playing two away international friendly matches against New Zealand later this week. The team in Dhaka is being guided by Under-23 coach Naushad Moosa.

. Major Asian stock markets surged today. South Korea’s Kospi snapped its three-day losing streak and ended 4.4 per cent higher.Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed almost 2.9 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex rose over two and a half per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index gained over 1.5 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng added more than 0.4 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite rose marginally.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose 1.3 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 gained 0.4 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone today. The Sensex rose 107 points or 0.13 per cent to close at 81,107. The Nifty gained 58 points or 0.23 per cent to settle at 25,045. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index added 0.6 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index rose marginally.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 2.2 per cent down at 90 US dollars and 51 cents per barrel.West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.8 per cent lower at 85 US dollars and 27 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. In the bullion market, gold and silver prices rebounded last week. The rise was supported by steep decline in crude oil prices over hopes of policy shifts following the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, concerns surrounding the global artificial intelligence sector also drove sharp flows from equity markets to commodity markets.At the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Gold futures for December contract gained nearly 2.7 percent to settle at 1 lakh 42 thousand 167 rupees per 10 grams during the week. Silver futures for December contract rose almost 3.2 percent to close at 1 lakh 84 thousand 787 rupees per kilogram.Meanwhile, at the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), Gold futures for the December contract jumped 4.5 percent during the week to settle at 4,074.9 dollars per troy ounce. Silver futures for the December contract climbed 5.4 percent over the week to end at 51.94 dollars per troy ounce.

. Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.

. Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has expressed confidence that India is on track to achieve its export target of one trillion dollars this year. Addressing the curtain-raiser event for the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 in New Delhi yesterday, Mr. Goyal said India had already achieved exports worth approximately 480 billion dollars in the first six months of the financial year, accounting for 48 per cent of the annual target. He said exports generally gain momentum in the second half of the year and expressed confidence in India’s overall export performance.Highlighting the contribution of the engineering sector, the Minister said exports from the sector had registered a growth of around 22 percent. He said the October export figures would be released by the Commerce Secretary on the 15th of this month and expressed optimism about the numbers. The Minister also emphasized that India should emerge as a global hub for technology development and design, with talent-driven solutions being developed within the country. He further said India should soon aim to achieve domestic sales of 10 million passenger vehicles, with exports being additional to domestic sales.Talking about the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027, the Commerce Minister said, bringing the entire mobility value chain together at one location made the event particularly attractive to international visitors, who could engage with different segments of the industry in a single visit. He emphasized that these platforms, which bring together entire value chains, enabled India to showcase its capabilities to the world.Mr. Goyal further said that the scale of the Indian market offered an ideal opportunity for global manufacturers to establish production facilities in India. The Minister also said that the mobility sector would be among the biggest beneficiaries of India’s position as the fastest-growing large economy.Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 will be held in February next year in New Delhi. The Expo will feature conferences, leadership sessions, policy discussions, product launches, and other similar interactions, bringing together experts and decision-makers from India and across the world.

. Union Health Minister J P Nadda has arrived in Colombo, Sri Lanka, to attend the first BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting to be held today. He was welcomed by India’s High Commissioner to Sri Lanka, Santosh Jha. In a social media post, Mr Nadda said he looks forward to engaging with health ministers of BIMSTEC member countries to strengthen regional health cooperation and advance shared public health priorities. He added that, guided by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of Neighbourhood First and Act East, India remains committed to building a healthier and more resilient BIMSTEC region.The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said in a separate post that the visit is an important step towards strengthening regional health cooperation and deepening India’s healthcare partnership with Sri Lanka and other BIMSTEC nations.

. Senior US lawmakers from both parties are pressing for tighter controls on the export of advanced American artificial intelligence chips to China. They warned that allegations involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang have heightened national security concerns.Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer has urged Congress to move quickly on three bipartisan bills designed to restrict China’s access to American technology. His call followed a joint statement by Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren and Republican Senator Jim Banks demanding stronger export controls. The renewed push comes as lawmakers consider including restrictions on advanced semiconductor technology in the annual defence policy legislation.Mr. Schumer called for passage of the AI OVERWATCH Act, the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act, arguing that Washington must prevent sensitive American technology from reaching potential adversaries. He also demanded an immediate briefing for the Senate and House intelligence committees on alleged Chinese efforts to obtain information from Nvidia and other American AI companies. He accused President Donald Trump of failing to adequately confront intelligence concerns.Senators Warren and Banks, both members of the Senate Banking Committee, said they had urged the Commerce Department in March to reconsider Nvidia’s export licences to China and conduct a comprehensive national security review. They alleged that Nvidia had subsequently received approvals to export hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips to China, including those companies with reported connections to the Chinese military.

. Minister of State for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh has emphasized the need to transform India’s scientific achievements into accessible and compelling narratives for the general public. Chairing the Second General Body Meeting of the Earth System Sciences Council in New Delhi yesterday, Dr. Singh called for greater citizen-centric science communication. The Minister stressed that scientific breakthroughs, technological innovations and research outcomes must be conveyed in simple language that enables ordinary citizens to appreciate their relevance and national significance.Reviewing the progress of the Deep Ocean Mission, Dr. Singh was apprised of major advances in India’s human deep-sea exploration program, including the development of MATSYA-6000, the country’s six thousand-meter-depth-rated human submersible. During the meeting, Dr. Singh reviewed scientific advances under Mission Mausam and the PRITHVI program, including developments in the Bharat Forecasting System, advanced numerical weather prediction and atmospheric observation networks.

. President Droupadi Murmu will confer Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 at a ceremony in New Delhi today. These awards honour India’s cleanest cities, celebrating their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban. Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal, and Minister of State of the Ministry, Tokhan Sahu will be present on the occasion.The Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 awards serve as a celebration of the collective achievements of cities and States and a renewed commitment to sustain on-ground achievements. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs informed that the 10th edition of the Swachh Survekshan on the theme of ‘Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel- Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath’ has been completed. It said that Swachh Survekshan has grown from 73 Urban Local Bodies in 2016 to more than four thousand cities in its latest edition.Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 introduced several key enhancements, including greater emphasis on citizen feedback, expanded coverage of Urban River Fronts, and focused indicators on prevention of open defecation and open urination and behaviour change initiatives in schools.As part of the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan, Urban Local Bodies were evaluated across 43 indicators spanning 10 key assessment areas. These include segregation, collection and transportation of waste, solid waste management, access to sanitation, overall welfare of sanitation workers and citizen feedback and grievance redressal.

. The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) conducted muhurat trading on the occasion of Diwali, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended today’s special trading session in the negative zone. The Sensex ended marginally lower by 29 points to close at 80 thousand 999, while the Nifty dipped 44 points, or 0.18 per cent to settle at 24 thousand 986. Conversely, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange ended with gains. The Midcap 100 index rose over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index jumped one per cent.

. The BJP today accused the Congress party of insulting Indian religion and culture. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi party MP and spokesperson Dr. Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed the statements given by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and Congress leader Imran Masood on the festival of Diwali. He claimed that it is clear that development is at the heart of the policies of BJP, while extremism and minority appeasement are at the heart of the opposition’s politics. Mr. Trivedi alleged that the Samajwadi Party and Congress have only two ways of doing politics, either insulting Hinduism or deceiving people in the name of Hinduism.Dr. Trivedi also hit out at the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, over his alleged ‘so-called dead economy’ remark for the Indian economy. The BJP Spokesperson said that on Dhanteras alone, this very economy demonstrated its strength by purchasing as much gold and silver on Dhanteras alone as the entire Europe purchases in three months.

. In Uttarakhand, the portals of Shri Kedarnath and Yamunotri Dham will be closed for the winter season today on the occasion of Bhai Dooj. With this, the annual summer pilgrimage to both shrines will come to an end. Preparations are underway for the closure of the temples. Our correspondent reports, both shrines have been decorated with quintals of flowers. The portals of Shri Kedarnath Dham, located in Rudraprayag district, will be closed at 8:30 this morning in accordance with Vedic rituals and religious traditions. The ceremonial palanquin of entered Following the closure, the ceremonial palanquin of Baba Kedar will proceed to the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath, the winter seat of Lord Kedarnath.The portals of Shri Yamunotri Dham in Uttarkashi district will be closed at 10:28 AM today. Thereafter, the ceremonial palanquin of Goddess Yamuna will proceed to Kharsali, her winter abode.  Over 64 lakh devotees have visited the Char Dham shrines this year, marking a record turnout. The portals of Shri Gangotri Dham were closed for the winter season yesterday on the occasion of the Annakoot festival.

. Today is National Education Day. The day is celebrated on this day every year in honour of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the first Education Minister of the country. This day highlights the importance of education in shaping India’s future. The central government has taken significant strides to promote access to education through various initiatives and constitutional provisions.On National Education Day today, Union Minister of Education Pralhad Joshi has reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to building an education system that is inclusive, equitable and future-ready. In a social media post, Mr Joshi said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is advancing towards an education framework that nurtures innovation and strengthens skills. The Minister added that this education framework also empowers every learner to contribute to the nation’s progress.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Anuj Shrivatri on becoming India’s 100th Chess Grandmaster, describing the achievement as a proud moment for the country. In a message on social media, the Prime Minister said India has reached a century in chess. He said the achievement reflects the immense talent, dedication and hard work of Indian chess players, as well as the growing popularity of the game among young people.The Prime Minister expressed hope that the milestone would inspire more youngsters to take up chess and strive for excellence. Anuj Shrivatri, who hails from Madhya Pradesh, achieved the milestone after winning the seventh ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in the Philippines on Sunday. With this achievement, India has reached the landmark of 100 Grandmasters. Chess legend Viswanathan Anand became the country’s first Grandmaster in 1988.India has added five Grandmasters between July and November this year. Before Anuj Shrivatri, Ethan Vaz, Harshvardhan G B, S Ashwath and V Rathnavel had earned the prestigious title. India is also home to reigning World Chess Champion D. Gukesh, who is set to defend his world title later this month.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura today. Similar conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep till tomorrow.IMD has advised fishermen to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea until Sunday, and also to stay away from the southeastern Bay of Bengal between the 13th and 15th of this month.Meanwhile, the Weather Agency has forecast a partly cloudy sky along with mist and shallow fog at most places in Delhi during the morning hours today. The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 299 as of 7 AM today.

. The Commanding Officers of two Japanese Maritime Self-Defense Force ships, JS Takanami and JS Kirisame, called on the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Indian Navy’s Western Naval Command, Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, during their goodwill visit to Mumbai.According to the Western Naval Command, the interaction provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange views on issues of mutual interest. The Western Naval Command said the goodwill visit reflects the shared commitment of both navies to deepen mutual understanding, strengthen maritime cooperation and work together towards a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

. India will provide a grant to expand Sri Lanka’s national emergency ambulance service, with the island’s cabinet approving a proposal to sign an agreement with New Delhi, a minister said yesterday. Sri Lanka’s Cabinet spokesperson and Minister Nalinda Jayathissa said the cabinet had approved the proposal to enter into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with India for the grant. India’s Health Minister J P Nadda, who arrived in Sri Lanka yesterday, will formalise the agreement today.The expansion will add 100 ambulances to the existing fleet of 322 vehicles operated by the country’s free emergency ambulance service, known as 1990 Suwa Seriya.The expansion follows a commitment made during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Sri Lanka in April 2025. The service was launched in 2016 with Indian grant assistance of USD 7.5 million and has since expanded into a nationwide emergency response network.

. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said that economic pressure on Iran had become so severe that President Donald Trump saw no immediate need for major combat operations, while warning that Washington remained ready to respond militarily if Tehran escalated. Rubio told reporters after a G-7 meeting that the combination of a blockade and sanctions was squeezing Iran’s oil earnings. He rejected suggestions that the absence of new major strikes amounted to a stalemate, arguing that the economic damage would deepen over time.Rubio said Iran was nearing the exhaustion of its oil supplies already at sea, adding that once these supplies run out, the country’s oil revenues would fall sharply. He also said that the United States was open to negotiations with Iran, but would not accept what he described as unrealistic demands from Tehran. Rubio said Qatar and other countries were continuing mediation efforts to facilitate a possible agreement.Meanwhile, he urged other countries to help protect commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz amid rising tensions in the region. On Lebanon, Rubio said Washington was holding direct talks between Lebanon and Israel and working towards arrangements for Israeli troop withdrawals and the deployment of Lebanese armed forces.

. In view of the Chhath festival, Northern Railway will operate 31 special trains from major railway stations in the Delhi region from today. The move is aimed at facilitating passengers travelling to their native places to celebrate the festival, particularly those heading towards eastern parts of the country.The Railways operated 27 special trains from major stations in the Delhi region yesterday. The Railways is also keeping a close watch on passenger movement and will operate additional special trains, as required. Senior railway officials are monitoring the situation at major railway stations.Meanwhile, preparations are in full swing at various Chhath ghats across Delhi. Elaborate arrangements are being made at more than 1400 Chhath ghats across Delhi this year. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta reviewed the preparations for Chhath Puja. She also directed concerned departments to ensure proper facilities for devotees. An 11-kilometre-long Chhath Ghat has been developed along the Munak Canal, stretching from the Outer Ring Road to Inderlok. BJP National President Nitin Nabin will inaugurate the grand Ghat tomorrow.Additionally, the Delhi Government also declared a public holiday on 16th of this month on account of Chhath Puja. Schools, colleges, government offices, autonomous bodies and public sector undertakings under the Delhi Government will remain closed on the day.

. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Women’s Selection Committee has announced squads for the upcoming all-format tour of South Africa in December. Smriti Mandhana is set to lead the side across all three formats.India will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is during the tour, which will begin with the Test match in Gqeberha on 9th December. The ODI series will start on 16th December in Paarl, followed by the second match in Cape Town on 19th December and the third in Bloemfontein on 22nd December. The three-match T20I series will begin on December 26 in Benoni. The second and third matches are scheduled to be played in Potchefstroom.Deepti Sharma has been named vice-captain of the Test and ODI squads, while Shafali Verma will serve as vice-captain in the T20I format. The Test squad features 15 players, including Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh, Yastika Bhatia, Sneh Rana and Kranti Gaud. The ODI squad also comprises 15 players, with Vaishnavi Sharma included in place of Sneh Rana from the Test squad. The T20I squad has 17 players, with Shafali Verma as vice-captain. Niki Prasad, G. Kamalini, Anushka Sharma, Prema Rawat, Amanjot Kaur, Renuka Singh Thakur and Arundhati Reddy are also part of the squad.

. Arunachal Pradesh’s Karateka Khyoda Talik has brought further recognition to the state by clinching a gold medal in the Male U21 Individual Kata category at the Commonwealth Karate Federation Club Championship 2026 held in Glasgow, Scotland.Congratulating the athlete on his achievement, Chief Minister Pema Khandu highlighted the growing presence of Arunachal’s sportspersons on the international stage.In a social media post, Khandu acknowledged the role of the Chief Minister’s Athlete Coaching and Empowerment Scheme (CM ACES) in nurturing young talents and providing them with opportunities and support to excel in competitive sports.

. In tennis, India’s Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale finished runners-up in the women’s doubles at the WTA 250 Chennai Open today. The Indian pair lost 2-6, 0-6 to Switzerland’s Simona Waltert and Naima Karamoko in the final.Despite the defeat in the title clash, Adkar and Bhosale made history by becoming the first all-Indian pair to reach a WTA Tour-level doubles final.Yesterday in the semifinals, the Indian duo defeated second seeds Weronika Falkowska and Alana Smith 6-2, 2-6, [10-8] to move into the final.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. India and France have discussed enhancing cooperation in supply chain resilience, critical technologies, cybersecurity and industrial partnerships. The discussions were held during the inaugural meeting of the India-France Economic Security and Critical Technologies Dialogue co-chaired by Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and Secretary General Martin Briens of the French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs in Paris yesterday.The External Affairs Ministry said both sides noted that the dialogue complemented the Innovation Roadmap 2030, the India-France Year of Innovation, the existing Economic and Financial Dialogue and the objective of doubling bilateral trade in the next five years. They agreed to work on the priorities identified during the dialogue.Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri concluded his two-day visit to France yesterday.  He undertook a comprehensive review of the India-France Special Global Strategic Partnership and the implementation of the Horizon 2047 Roadmap with Secretary General Briens as a part of his visit. Their discussions covered key areas of bilateral cooperation, as well as India-EU relations. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global issues of mutual interest and cooperation in multilateral fora.The visit reflects the continued regular high-level exchanges between India and France and the shared commitment of both sides to further deepen their Special Global Strategic Partnership.

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight.Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.An orange alert has been issued for very heavy rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.Thunderstorms accompanied by hail are likely over East Rajasthan, Haryana, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand and West Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms and gusty winds are also forecast in several other states, including Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam and Meghalaya.Meanwhile Delhi witnessed light to moderate rainfall this evening. The IMD has forecast very light rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow morning.The maximum temperature is expected to remain between 26 and 28 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature is likely to range from 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.

. Most Asian stock markets ended on a mixed note today. South Korea’s Kospi fell 0.8 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index declined 2.2 per cent and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng edged down marginally. Conversely, Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed over 2.3 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex rose nearly five per cent and China’s Shanghai Composite gained 0.3 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose nearly one per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 gained 0.8 per cent, when reports last came in.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers of Indian equities during the first week of November. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested 38,971 crore rupees in the domestic stock market, marking a reversal in investment flows. Of the total investment, 38 thousand 519 crore rupees came through purchases on stock exchanges, while 452 crore rupees were invested through the primary market.The shift in FPI’s sentiment was due to sharp sell-off in global technology stocks, triggered by concerns over artificial intelligence-related investments and a possible slowdown in data centre spending. The recent correction in global AI stocks has made Indian equities more attractive to overseas investors.Meanwhile, the debt market witnessed net inflows of 4,319 crore rupees in November so far.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. The United States House of Representatives has rejected a resolution seeking the impeachment of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over his conduct in office and handling of the ongoing war in Iran. The resolution, moved by Republican Congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky and supported by Democrats, was defeated on Tuesday after President Donald Trump expressed strong support for the Defence Secretary. Most Republican lawmakers stood by Mr. Hegseth.The vote comes amid growing political challenges for the Republican Party following significant losses in the midterm elections. The war in Iran and the resulting rise in fuel prices have emerged as major issues of concern within the party.The rejection of the resolution may, however, provide only temporary relief to Mr. Hegseth, as Democrats are expected to gain control of both chambers of Congress in January, potentially renewing efforts to hold the Defence Secretary accountable.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading three and a half per cent down at 94 US dollars and 92 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 2.8 per cent lower at 87 US dollars and seven cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The Government has invited fresh applications under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices, known as PLI-MD 2.0. The scheme has been extended up to 2035-36, with a total outlay of around two thousand seven hundred crore rupees. The online application portal is expected to become operational within the next ten days.The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers said several changes have been introduced in the scheme based on the experience gained during its first phase. These include simplified eligibility conditions and an easier procedure for claiming incentives.Under the revised scheme, applicants will get three years to establish manufacturing facilities in any of the four target segments. These include medical consumables, disposables and implants; critical components; high-end medical devices with limited domestic manufacturing; and high-end devices that are currently only assembled in the country. The government has also removed the minimum sales threshold for claiming incentives and reduced the minimum investment requirement.To improve ease of doing business, companies can submit multiple applications across one or more target segments. The application window will also remain open continuously for an extended period. The initiative aims to strengthen domestic manufacturing of medical devices and promote investment in the sector.

. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has described the first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, the United States and Russia in Abu Dhabi as constructive and substantive. In a post on social media, Zelensky said the discussions focused on humanitarian issues, including the release of prisoners, security guarantees for Ukraine and measures to de-escalate the conflict.He said he had given fresh instructions to the Ukrainian negotiating team for the second day of talks. The two-day meeting is the first trilateral engagement between the three countries since February. US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are also participating. Meanwhile, reports of civilian casualties in attacks in the Russia-Ukraine conflict continue to emerge.
